title_original: The Risk of AI-Powered Antidetect Browsers in Online Fraud and Influence Operations
description: Online platforms rely on digital signals to identify suspicious accounts and activity. Antidetect browsers make those signals harder to trust by allowing operators to create and manage large numbers of browser profiles that appear to belong to different users, devices and locations. While these tools have legitimate uses, Check Point Research found documented evidence of their use in criminal ecosystems for activities including account takeover and payment fraud. AI and automation can further increase the scale of these operations. Key Findings Antidetect browsers allow operators to manage large numbers of isolated browser profiles that appear to come from different users, devices […]The postThe Risk of AI-Powered Antidetect Browsers in Online Fraud and Influence Operationsappeared first onCheck Point Blog.
